full_judgment: 9. Mr Gazi Md Neamat Hossain, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, assails the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners on the ground that the petitioner's application is not maintainable as the petitioner did not file counter-statement under section 15 of the Trade Marks Act read with Rule 32 and, as such, his application would be deemed to be abandoned. He further submits that it is not physically possible for the Registrar to give notice to all the applicants. The learned Advocate further argues that an applicant can come for rectification if he is the true owner of a Trade Mark even though it is registered in other's name. But in this case the petitioner does not claim to be the true owner of the Trade Mark, he only claims that he is the first user of the Trade Mark in Bangladesh but no evidence has been adduced in support of such claim. As the petitioner has failed to make out a case in respect of the ownership of the Trade Mark the application should fail. The burden of proof is on the petitioner but he has failed to adduce any evidence to show that he is the true owner. The learned Advocate further submits that he has already filed a criminal case and if in that case it is proved that he is the true owner, no rectification will be necessary.
